en: Ishaq ibn 'Umar ibn Salit narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Kinanah ibn Nu'aym, from Abu Barzah, that the Prophet (pbuh) was in an expedition and Allah granted him spoils of war. He said to his Companions, "Are you missing anyone?" They said, "Yes, so-and-so, so-and-so, and so-and-so." Then he said, "Are you missing anyone?" They said, "Yes, so-and-so, so-and-so, and so-and-so." Then he said, "Are you missing anyone?" They said, "No." He said, "But I miss Julaybib, so seek him." So he was searched for among the slain, and they found him beside seven whom he had killed, and then they killed him. The Prophet (pbuh) came, stood over him, and said, "He killed seven, then they killed him. This man is of me and I am of him; this man is of me and I am of him." He said: Then he placed him upon his forearms—he had no bed except the forearms of the Prophet (pbuh). He said: So a grave was dug for him and he was placed in his grave. And he did not mention any washing.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to us, Zakariyya' ibn 'Adi narrated to us, 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Amr informed us, from 'Abd al-Karim, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, who said: "My father was brought on the day of Uhud mutilated, and placed before the Prophet (pbuh)..." and he mentioned the like of their hadith.

Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar narrated to us—both of them from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, with this hadith, except that in the hadith of Ibn Jurayj there is no mention of the angels or the weeping of the weeping woman.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: My father was struck down on the day of Uhud, so I began uncovering the cloth from his face and weeping, and they began forbidding me while the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) did not forbid me. He said: And Fatimah bint 'Amr began weeping over him, so the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "Whether she weeps over him or does not weep over him, the angels continued to shade him with their wings until you lifted him up."

Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar al-Qawariri and 'Amr al-Naqid both narrated to us from Sufyan—'Ubaydullah said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us—he said: I heard Ibn al-Munkadir saying: I heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah saying: On the day of Uhud, my father was brought covered with a garment, having been mutilated. He said: I wanted to uncover the garment, but my people forbade me; then I wanted to uncover the garment, but my people forbade me. So the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) lifted it—or ordered it and it was lifted—and he heard the voice of a weeping woman or screaming woman. He said: "Who is this?" They said: "The daughter of 'Amr—or sister of 'Amr." He said: "Why does she weep? The angels continued to shade him with their wings until he was lifted."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, 'Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) took a sword on the day of Uhud and said: "Who will take this from me?" They stretched out their hands, every person among them saying: "I will, I will." He said: "Who will take it with its due right?" He said: The people hesitated. Then Simak ibn Kharashah, Abu Dujanah, said: "I will take it with its due right." He said: So he took it and cleaved with it the crowns of the idolaters' heads.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated it to us, Salim ibn Nuh narrated to us, 'Umar ibn 'Amir narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, that Ukaydir of Dumat al-Jandal gifted a robe to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh)... and he mentioned similarly, but he did not mention in it: "and he used to prohibit silk."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us, Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Shayban narrated to us, from Qatadah, Anas ibn Malik narrated to us that a robe of fine silk was gifted to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh)—and he used to prohibit silk—so the people marveled at it. He said: "By the One in Whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the handkerchiefs of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh in Paradise are better than this."
Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Jabalah narrated to us, Umayyah ibn Khalid narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, this hadith with both chains of narration together, like the narration of Abu Dawud.

Ahmad ibn 'Abdah al-Dabbi narrated to us, Abu Dawud narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, Abu Ishaq informed me, he said: I heard al-Bara' ibn 'Azib saying: A silk garment was brought to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh)... and he mentioned the hadith. Then Ibn 'Abdah said: Abu Dawud informed us, Shu'bah narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to me, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (pbuh), with something like this, or the like of it.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara' saying: A silk suit was gifted to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh), so his Companions began touching it and marveling at its softness. He said: "Do you marvel at the softness of this? The handkerchiefs of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh in Paradise are better than it and softer."

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah al-Ruzzi narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' al-Khaffaf narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, Anas ibn Malik narrated to us that the Prophet of Allah (pbuh) said while his bier was placed—meaning Sa'd: "The Throne of the Most Merciful shook for it."

Amr al-Naqid narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Idris al-Awdi narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "The Throne of the Most Merciful shook for the death of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh."

Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah saying: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said while the bier of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh was before them: "The Throne of the Most Merciful shook for it."

Abu Dawud, Sulayman ibn Ma'bad, narrated to me, 'Amr ibn 'Asim narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to us, who said: I asked Anas ibn Malik, "Who collected the Quran during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh)?" He said: "Four, all of them from the Ansar: Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Mu'adh ibn Jabal, Zayd ibn Thabit, and a man from the Ansar with the kunyah Abu Zayd."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Abu Dawud narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: I heard Anas saying: Four collected the Quran during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh), all of them from the Ansar: Mu'adh ibn Jabal, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Zayd ibn Thabit, and Abu Zayd. Qatadah said: I asked Anas, "Who is Abu Zayd?" He said, "One of my paternal uncles."

Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, with this chain of narration, and he added: Shu'bah said: "He started with these two; I do not know with which of the two he started."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Ibrahim, from Masruq, who said: Ibn Mas'ud was mentioned in the presence of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, and he said: "That is a man I will never cease to love after hearing the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) say: 'Learn the recitation of the Quran from four: from Ibn Mas'ud, Salim the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and Mu'adh ibn Jabal.'"

Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us—they said: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us; (H) and Bishr ibn Khalid narrated to me, Muhammad—meaning Ibn Ja'far—informed us—both of them from Shu'bah, from al-A'mash, with their chain of narration; and they differed from Shu'bah regarding the sequence of the four.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb both narrated to us—they said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, with the chain of Jarir and Waki'. In the narration of Abu Bakr from Abu Mu'awiyah, he mentioned Mu'adh before Ubayy; and in the narration of Abu Kurayb, Ubayy before Mu'adh.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us—they said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from Masruq, who said: We were with 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr and we mentioned a hadith from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. He said: "Indeed, that is a man I will never cease to love after something I heard the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) say. I heard him say: 'Recite the Quran from four persons: from Ibn Umm 'Abd'—and he started with him—'and from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and from Salim the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, and from Mu'adh ibn Jabal.'" And a wording that Zuhayr did not mention was his statement: "saying it."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr both narrated to us—they said: Waki' narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Shaqiq, from Masruq, who said: We used to visit 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr and converse with him—and Ibn Numayr said: in his presence—and one day we mentioned 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. He said: "You have mentioned a man whom I will never cease to love after something I heard from the Messenger of Allah (pbuh). I heard the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) say: 'Take the Quran from four: from Ibn Umm 'Abd'—and he started with him—'and Mu'adh ibn Jabal, and Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and Salim the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah.'"

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, Qutbah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, from 'Abdullah, who said: "By the One besides Whom there is no god, there is no surah from the Book of Allah except that I know where it was revealed, and there is no verse except that I know concerning what it was revealed. And if I knew of anyone who was more knowledgeable of the Book of Allah than me whom camels could reach, I would ride to him."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated to us, 'Abdah ibn Sulayman informed us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Shaqiq, from 'Abdullah, that he recited: "And whoever defrauds will come with what he took on the Day of Resurrection." Then he said: "Upon whose recitation do you order me to recite? By Allah, I recited directly to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) seventy-some surahs, and the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) certainly know that I am the most knowledgeable of them regarding the Book of Allah; and if I knew of anyone more knowledgeable than me, I would travel to him." Shaqiq said: "So I sat in the circles of the Companions of Muhammad (pbuh), and I did not hear anyone refute that against him or find fault with him."

Al-Qasim ibn Zakariyya' narrated to me, 'Ubaydullah—he is Ibn Musa—narrated to us, from Shayban, from al-A'mash, from Malik ibn al-Harith, from Abu al-Ahwas, who said: I came to Abu Musa and found 'Abdullah and Abu Musa; (H) and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abi 'Ubaydah narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Zayd ibn Wahb, who said: I was sitting with Hudhayfah and Abu Musa... and he related the hadith, and the hadith of Qutbah is more complete and longer.

Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us, Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, Qutbah—he is Ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz—narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Malik ibn al-Harith, from Abu al-Ahwas, who said: We were in the house of Abu Musa with a group of the companions of 'Abdullah while they were looking at a copy of the Mus-haf. Then 'Abdullah stood up, and Abu Mas'ud said: "I do not know that the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) left behind anyone more knowledgeable of what Allah revealed than this man who just stood up." Abu Musa said: "Indeed, if you say that, he used to be present when we were absent, and permission was granted to him when we were screened."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Abu al-Ahwas saying: I was present with Abu Musa and Abu Mas'ud when Ibn Mas'ud died, and one of them said to his companion: "Do you think he left behind anyone like him?" He said: "If you say that, he was indeed granted permission when we were screened, and he was present when we were absent."

Zuhayr ibn Harb, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us—they said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Aswad, from Abu Musa, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) while I considered 'Abdullah to be of the members of the household—or what he mentioned similar to this.

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated it to me, Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Ishaq, that he heard al-Aswad saying: I heard Abu Musa saying: "My brother and I arrived from Yemen..." and he mentioned the like of it.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali and Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn Rafi's—Ishaq said: informed us, and Ibn Rafi' said: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Aswad ibn Yazid, from Abu Musa, who said: My brother and I arrived from Yemen, and for some time we did not consider Ibn Mas'ud and his mother to be anything other than members of the household of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh), because of their frequent entering upon him and their constancy with him.
